land.text: Eshnunna and its Diyala district, an Ur III province under governors such as Urguedinna and Ituria

predecessors.note: The Eshnunna page: Shu-iliya "in 2026 BC got rid of the Ur III calendar". The third-dynasty-of-ur dossier (me-01) books the loss at -2020, six years later (that page gives no year).

land.text: Eshnunna and its Diyala, Arrapha and Euphrates lands

successors.note: "The Babylonians occupied the city of Eshnunna" in Hammurabi's year 31 (1762 BC). A rebel king Iluni followed c. 1742-1731 (not mapped).

capitals.name: Eshnunna (Tell Asmar)
capitals.note: Page coordinates 33.48417 N, 44.72833 E; "the capital is the tell of Tell Asmar in Diyala Governorate".

rulers.name: Shu-iliya
rulers.note: First lugal; the page gives no reign length.

rulers.name: Silli-Sin
rulers.note: "installed by Eshnunnian troops"; the page gives c. 1764-1756, beyond the dossier end of 1762.

correction.text: Eshnunna (Tell Asmar) and its district on the lower Diyala, independent of Ur from 2026 BC

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -2026..-1901: no Cliopatria shape. The page gives the capital (Tell Asmar) and says the extent "was less than under Ur III"; independence in 2026 BC. Drawn as the city and its district, a reading, not a mapped frontier.

correction.text: Eshnunna with Ishur, Tutub and Nerebtum on the lower Diyala

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1900..-1829: "Warassa (Warissa) conquers Ishur, Tutub, and Nerebtum (Kiti, at Tell Ishchali)" c. 1900 BC; these lie on the lower Diyala near modern Baghdad (my reading; the page gives no map).

correction.text: the Diyala region, Tutub and Nerebtum, Arrapha (Kirkuk) in the north and Rapiqum on the Euphrates

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1828..-1773: Ipiq-Adad II "took Arrapha to the north", consolidated the Diyala region, and took Rapiqum on the Euphrates and the Suhum region (undated); Eshnunna page: his conquests "brought the Diyala region under Eshnunna's control". The Dadusha page adds Shaduppum and Dur-Rimush as inherited, Mankisum seized (undated, unlocated). Kirkuk stands for Arrapha; Rapiqum is drawn as a circle on the Euphrates west of Baghdad (my reading, the pages give no coordinates).

correction.text: the core plus Assur, Ekallatum and Qattara on the Tigris and Subat-Enlil (Shubat-Enlil, Tell Leilan) on the Khabur plain

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1772..-1767: "In c. 1772 BC, the new king of Eshnunna, Ibal-pi-el II invaded Ishme-Dagan's kingdom, occupying Assur, Ekallatum and Qattare before seizing Shamshi-Adad's old capital at Shubut-Enlil." The core is unchanged.

correction.text: the core of Eshnunna under Elam and then Silli-Sin; the northern holdings are not on the pages

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1766..-1762: Elam conquered Eshnunna around 1767 ("conquering it and imposed direct rule from his sukkal Kudu-zulush in Susa"; Ibal-pi-el II killed c. 1765) and Silli-Sin was installed c. 1764. The page says nothing about the land under Silli-Sin; the core of the previous keyframes is kept, with Assur and Subat-Enlil dropped (page silent: unverified).

ledger.note: c. 2026 BC: Shu-iliya makes Eshnunna independent of Ur. "Shu-iliya drops the Ur III calendar, calls himself lugal, and is listed as gaining independence from Ibbi-Sin"; the page: "in 2026 BC got rid of the Ur III calendar". Year from the page; the land is my reading (Tell Asmar and its district). The third-dynasty-of-ur dossier has -2020.

region.text: the city of Eshnunna, briefly seized by Subartu

ledger.note: c. 2011 BC (derived): Subartu seizes Eshnunna. The page has Eshnunna independent as the state of Warum "for about 15 years" after 2026, then "Subartu briefly seizes the city"; 2026 minus 15 gives 2011, the page dates no seizure.
c. 2010 BC: Ishbi-Erra of Isin "defeats Subartu and installs Nur-ahum". The page does not call Nur-ahum a vassal of Isin.

region.text: Ishur, Tutub and Nerebtum on the lower Diyala

ledger.counterpart: Ishur, Tutub and Nerebtum (city-states on the lower Diyala)
ledger.note: c. 1900 BC: "Warassa (Warissa) conquers Ishur, Tutub, and Nerebtum (Kiti, at Tell Ishchali)". The Ipiq-Adad II page has Ipiq-Adad II "defeated Sin-abushu of Nerebtum" c. 1828 and annexing Tutub, so the 1900 conquest did not hold, or the pages disagree; the land (the lower Diyala near Baghdad) is my reading.

region.text: Shaduppum (Tell Harmal) on the edge of modern Baghdad

ledger.note: c. 1855 BC: Ipiq-Adad II takes Shaduppum. The page has the campaign against Aminum c. 1857, "attempting to seize Shaduppum" (Tell Harmal): "first defeated, but won the second confrontation two years later"; the Dadusha page counts Shaduppum among the lands "brought under Eshnunna by his father, Ipiq-Adad II".

region.text: Arrapha to the north, Uzarlulu and the Diyala region

ledger.note: c. 1828 BC: Ipiq-Adad II takes Arrapha. He "took Arrapha to the north" and then defeated Sin-abushu of Nerebtum "to consolidate the Diyala region", annexing Uzarlulu and Tutub in the same campaign. Arrapha is Kirkuk (my reading).

region.text: Rapiqum on the Euphrates and the lands up river to Suhum, drawn as a circle

ledger.note: c. 1828 BC (bridged to the Arrapha campaign): Rapiqum, Suhum and Me-Turan. The page lists them undated: "Rapiqum was taken, his first city on the Euphrates", "Eshnunna expanded up the Euphrates to the Suhum region, bordering Mari", "Me-Turan was taken"; the reign is c. 1862-1818 and the page dates no conquest. The Eshnunna page's table has Ipiq-Adad II conquering Rapiqum, Suhum, Me-Turan and Arrapha.

region.text: Mahazum, a district on the Diyala River (location approximate)

ledger.note: c. 1776 BC: Ibal-pi-El II seizes Mahazum. Year-name 4: "Ibal-pi-El seized the land of Mahazum", a district on the Diyala River; the page gives no coordinates, so the whole Diyala governorate is shown as a stand-in.

c. 1772 BC: Eshnunna occupies Assur. "In c. 1772 BC, the new king of Eshnunna, Ibal-pi-el II invaded Ishme-Dagan's kingdom, occupying Assur, Ekallatum and Qattare". The Eshnunna page puts the taking of Assur and Ekallatum under Ibal-pi-El II without a year.

region.text: Subat-Enlil (Shubat-Enlil, Tell Leilan), Shamshi-Adad I's old capital

ledger.note: c. 1772 BC: Eshnunna seizes Subat-Enlil. "... before seizing Shamshi-Adad's old capital at Shubut-Enlil." The Eshnunna page: Eshnunna "takes Shubat-Enlil". Mirrors the assyria loss.

region.text: Suhum on the middle Euphrates between Mari and Hit, drawn as two circles

ledger.note: Fall 1772 BC: the Mari-Eshnunna conflict. Zimri-Lim's page: "The Mari-Eshnunna conflict erupted in the fall of 1772, when Eshnunna invaded Suhum." The Ibal-pi-El II page has Rapiqum destroyed c. 1771.

1770 BC: peace. "Peace: it was concluded in 1770. Zimri-Lim recognized Ibal-pi-El as his father, and regained the lost territories." Eshnunna's forces had been defeated at Andarig (the page dates it not).

region.text: Eshnunna and its land under Elamite rule

ledger.note: c. 1767 BC: Elam takes Eshnunna. "Elam, under Siwe-palar-huppak, takes Eshnunna in Zimri-Lim's 9th year"; the Ibal-pi-El II page: around 1767 he led a coalition against Eshnunna, "conquering it and imposed direct rule from his sukkal Kudu-zulush in Susa", and has Ibal-pi-El II killed c. 1765 (it calls its own dating inconsistent). The Zimri-Lim page has the capture in 1765. The elam dossier (me-01) also has -1767.

c. 1767 BC (bridged): the occupation of Assur ends. The pages do not say when Eshnunna left Assur and Subat-Enlil; Eshnunna was conquered by Elam around 1767 and Ishme-Dagan I (d. c. 1765) "retained control only of Ekallatum" (Old Assyrian period). Mirrors the assyria dossier.
c. 1767 BC (bridged): Subat-Enlil is no longer Eshnunna's. The pages say nothing about Subat-Enlil after c. 1772; shown as lost with the Elamite conquest. Page silent.

c. 1764 BC: Silli-Sin is "installed by Eshnunnian troops" and reigns c. 1764-1756; "He makes a treaty with Hammurabi and marries Hammurabi's daughter." The elam dossier (me-01) ends its occupation at -1760 ("Around 1760 BC, Hammurabi drove out the Elamites").

region.text: the whole of Eshnunna, occupied by Babylon

ledger.note: 1762 BC (Hammurabi year 31): "the Babylonians occupied the city of Eshnunna". The page then has the idol of Assur returned and, in Hammurabi's year 38, a flood destroying Eshnunna. Zimri-Lim's page: in 1762 Babylon captured Eshnunna and Zimri-Lim reportedly sided with Eshnunna.

wars.name: Ipiq-Adad II against Aminum and Shaduppum
wars.outcome: Ipiq-Adad II was first defeated, "but won the second confrontation two years later"; Shaduppum was Eshnunna's afterwards (Dadusha page).
wars.note: The Eshnunna page calls Aminum "of Assur"; the Ipiq-Adad II page names him without a city.

wars.name: Elamite invasion in Ipiq-Adad II's reign
wars.outcome: "Invaded again, this time by the Elamites around 1823 BC"; the page does not say how it ended. A year-name has Elamites defeated.

wars.name: Qabra campaign with Shamshi-Adad I

zones.text: the area between the two Zab Rivers, Erbil plain

wars.outcome: "Around 1781 BC, the coalition with Dadusha and Shamshi-Adad I besieged the city"; Qabarum became a provincial centre in Shamshi-Adad's kingdom, not Eshnunna's.

wars.name: Eshnunna against Ishme-Dagan I and Mari
wars.outcome: Eshnunna occupied Assur, Ekallatum, Qattara and Subat-Enlil c. 1772 and invaded Suhum in fall 1772; defeated at Andarig; peace with Mari 1770.
wars.note: Dates from the Old Assyrian period and Zimri-Lim pages.

wars.name: Elamite conquest of Eshnunna
wars.outcome: Siwe-Palar-Khuppak "conquering it and imposed direct rule from his sukkal Kudu-zulush in Susa"; Ibal-pi-El II killed c. 1765.
wars.note: The page dates the conquest both c. 1767 and c. 1765.

wars.name: Babylonian occupation of Eshnunna
wars.outcome: "The Babylonians occupied the city of Eshnunna" in Hammurabi's year 31 (1762 BC).

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the extent is the city and the districts the pages name. The kingdom was "one of the most powerful states in the Mesopotamian region in the early 18th century BC" (Dadusha page).

notes:
SCOPE. State Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names empty; every keyframe new). Years -2026..-1762 from the Eshnunna page (independence 2026; Babylonian occupation 1762, Hammurabi year 31). A rebel kingdom under Iluni c. 1742-1731 (Samsu-iluna years 19/20) is on the page; it is not mapped and Anni and Ahu-sina are listed as later kings; the 12th-century conquest by Shutruk-Nakhunte of Elam is Elam's event (me-01).
PAGES. Six pages (Eshnunna, Ipiq-Adad II, Dadusha, Ibal-pi-El II, Old Assyrian period, Zimri-Lim). The brief allows 2-5; the last two are shared with the assyria and lim-dynasty-of-mari dossiers, where they are also counted.
MAPPING. The pages give one coordinate (Tell Asmar). Every other place is my reading of a name: Ishur, Tutub, Nerebtum on the lower Diyala near Baghdad; Arrapha = Kirkuk; Rapiqum on the Euphrates west of Baghdad (circle at 43.4 E, 33.5 N); Suhum two circles on the middle Euphrates; Mahazum shown as the whole Diyala governorate. Gazetteer names missing: Eshnunna (Tell Asmar), Tutub, Nerebtum, Shaduppum, Rapiqum, Suhum, Arrapha, Ekallatum, Qattara, Subat-Enlil, Mahazum.
DISAGREEMENTS. (1) Independence: Eshnunna page 2026; third-dynasty-of-ur dossier (me-01) -2020 (no year on its page). (2) Nerebtum and Tutub: Eshnunna page has Warassa conquering them c. 1900, the Ipiq-Adad II page has Ipiq-Adad II beating Sin-abushu of Nerebtum and annexing Tutub c. 1828; both are kept and no loss is dated between. (3) Aminum: "of Assur" on the Eshnunna page, unqualified on the Ipiq-Adad II page. (4) The Elamite conquest: c. 1767 vs c. 1765 on one page. (5) Elam ends its occupation at -1760 in the elam dossier (me-01); here -1764 (Silli-Sin installed) and the dissolution in -1762; the elam dossier should end by -1762. (6) Laws of Eshnunna: Naram-Sin or Dadusha (page inconsistent), not used. (7) Hammurabi's "flood" year-name (year 38) is after the dissolution and is not an event.
UNDATED, NOT IN LEDGER. Dadusha seized Mankisum and defeated the troops of Ekallatum (year-names, unlocated, undated); Ilum-muttabbil of Der "may have taken Eshnunna" (page hedges); Ibal-pi-El II seized Syupur-Szamasz and Astabala (Upper Euphrates, near Birecik, c. 1767 per the Ibal-pi-El II page) and Diniktum and Rapiqum; the Rapiqum destruction c. 1771.
MIRRORS. assyria (occupation -1772 to -1767, loss of Subat-Enlil -1772); lim-dynasty-of-mari (contest -1772 to -1770 over Suhum); babylonia (gain -1762); elam (occupation -1767 to -1764; elam says -1760); third-dynasty-of-ur (loss, -2020 there). Isin (Ishbi-Erra installs Nur-ahum c. 2010) has no mirror: the page does not call Nur-ahum a vassal.
